identity.name: House of Anjou-Sicily
alt_names: Angevin Kingdom of Albania and Achaea
Capetian Angevins in Greece and Albania

land.text: the Albanian coast of the 1279 Cliopatria shape, from Durrës south to Butrint

predecessors.note: 'He took the title of King of Albania in February 1272'; the territory came 'from the Despotate of Epirus' in 1271 (Capetian House of Anjou page). Corfu was Manfred's widow's dowry, seized by Charles's troops before the end of 1268 (Charles I of Anjou page).

land.text: the Principality of Achaea as in Cliopatria's 1385 shape

successors.note: 'In 1383, Achaea was annexed by Charles III of Naples, and James of Baux was driven away'; a Vicary government under the Durazzo kings followed from 1383 to 1396 and the Angevins held the principality until the purchase of 1404 (Principality of Achaea page). Cliopatria keeps this row to 1384.

land.text: Corfu, which stayed with the dynasty until Venice took it in 1386

successors.note: Corfu page: 'From 1386, Corfu was controlled by the Republic of Venice'; a bridge for 1383-1385, the pages name no holder.

capitals.name: Durrës (Durazzo)
capitals.note: Kingdom of Albania infobox: 'Capital: Durazzo (Dyrrhachium, modern Durrës)'; the kingdom 'had its own structure and organs of government which was located in Durrës' (undated). Naples, the dynasty's seat (14.27 E, 40.85 N), lies outside every shape of this row and is not used.

capitals.name: Corfu
capitals.note: Durrës is Byzantine (1288) and then Serbian (1296-1304); no page names a seat for these years. Corfu is the one place of the shape held and governed ('from 1286 to 1290 ... by Richard Orsini on behalf of the Kingdom and then by Florent of Hainaut'): a reading, not a statement of the page.

capitals.name: Durrës (Durazzo)
capitals.note: 'Angevin forces regained control' of Durrës in September 1304 and 'the Angevins held Durazzo until 1368'.

capitals.name: Corfu
capitals.note: Durrës is lost to Karl Thopia in 1368. The Achaea page names no capital for the Angevin years (infobox: Andravida 1205-1249, Mystras 1249-1261); Corfu is the one place of the shape that stayed with the dynasty until 1386 (a reading).

union.text: the Albanian coast of the 1279 Cliopatria shape, from Durrës south to Butrint

correction.text: Corfu and the Albanian coast from Durrës to Butrint, 1272-1278 (Berat lost 1274, ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 242.8 km2 (a patch at Corfu town) for 1272-1278. 'The Kingdom of Albania was declared in late February 1272' (Charles I proclaimed 21 February 1272) and 'ran from the Durazzo region south along the coast to Butrint', with 'poorly defined' borders; Berat fell to the Byzantines in 1274. Charles inherited Achaea only on 1 May 1278 (ledger), so it is not in this shape. The Albanian coast of the later shape is added to the earlier years, a soft reading.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1279-1281 only: the interior of Albania is lost by 1282, Malta in July 1283, Durrës in 1288 and Achaea in 1289 (new keyframes _1282, _1283, _1288, _1289)

keyframe_review.note: 31,264 km2 for 1279-1284 in Cliopatria: Achaea (Cliopatria's Principality of Achaea row, 14,593 km2 in 1260-1278, has a gap exactly in 1279-1293), the Albanian coast, Corfu and Malta (the bbox reaches 35.77 N, 14.34 E). Charles 'inherited the Principality of Achaea from William II of Villehardouin, who had died on 1 May 1278' and ruled it through baillis ('he would never personally visit it', Achaea page). In March 1279 Nikephoros I surrendered the castles of Sopot and Butrint to him (ledger). The shape holds only to 1281: the Byzantine counteroffensive 'drove the Angevins out of the interior by 1282' (Capetian House page; the Kingdom of Albania page says 'by 1281'), Malta went to Aragon in July 1283 and the shape then shrinks step by step. No area figure on the pages. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1279..1281 from this entry's own 'valid 1279-1281 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

minus.text: the Albanian interior outside the coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint

correction.text: the 1279 shape without the Albanian interior, which the Byzantines took 'by 1282'; Malta, Corfu, Achaea and the coastal strongholds remain

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1282: 'A Byzantine counteroffensive soon ensued, which drove the Angevins out of the interior by 1282' (the Kingdom of Albania page: 'by 1281'); the kingdom 'was soon reduced ... to a small area centered around Durrës'.

union.text: the Albanian interior outside the coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint

correction.text: the 1279 shape without the Albanian interior and without Malta (Roger of Lauria received the homage of the island on 8 July 1283)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1283-1284: Malta (316 km2) leaves in July 1283 although Cliopatria keeps it to 1284; the rest as in 1282.

minus.text: the Albanian interior outside the coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint

correction.text: the 1285 shape without the Albanian interior, valid 1285-1287: Achaea, Corfu, Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint remain; Durrës goes in 1288 and Achaea in 1289 (new keyframes _1288 and _1289)

keyframe_review.note: 30,957 km2 for 1285-1293 in Cliopatria: the step of -307 km2 from 1279 is Malta's area (316 km2) leaving. Cliopatria's shape still holds the Albanian interior, lost by 1282 (ledger), and runs to 1293, but the Byzantines took Durrës in 1288 ('Durrës fell in Byzantine hands in 1288') and Charles II granted Achaea to Isabelle of Villehardouin and Florent of Hainaut in 1289, so the shape is valid, without the interior, for 1285-1287 only; 1289-1293 is the coastal patch of 1294 plus Butrint (new keyframe _1289).

union.text: the Albanian interior outside the coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint

correction.text: the 1285 shape without the Albanian interior and without Durrës, which fell to the Byzantines in 1288; Achaea, Corfu, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint remain

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1288: 'Durrës fell in Byzantine hands in 1288'; Achaea is still Angevin until the grant of 1289.

correction.text: Corfu, Butrint and Kaninë/Vlorë: Cliopatria's 1294 coastal patch drawn from 1289, plus Butrint ('Corfu and Butrint remained in Angevin hands at least up to 1292'; 'Kaninë castle was the last to fall to the Byzantines probably in 1294')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1289-1293: Achaea is granted away in 1289 (Principality of Achaea page: 'not long after his release and coronation in 1289') and Durrës is Byzantine, so what remains is the coast of Vlorë and Kaninë, Corfu and Butrint. The Corfu page has Corfu governed 'from 1286 to 1290 by Richard Orsini on behalf of the Kingdom and then by Florent of Hainaut'. The 1294 patch covers 1,012 km2 by the gazetteer (four cells); Butrint is not in it and is added.

union.text: Cliopatria's 1294 patch without Vlorë and Kaninë

correction.text: the coastal patch without Vlorë and Kaninë, 1294-1303: Corfu and Butrint remain

keyframe_review.note: 725 km2 for 1294-1325 (the same coastal patch as Cliopatria's later Principality of Valona, bbox 39.58-40.74 N). Kaninë 'the last Angevin holdout, falling probably in 1294', Corfu and Butrint 'stayed Angevin at least until 1292'; Durrës was Byzantine from 1288, Serbian from 1296 and Angevin again after 1304. Corrected for 1294-1303 by dropping the Vlorë/Kaninë area; 1304 onward uses the new keyframe house-of-anjou-sicily_1304. Butrint is added (Cliopatria's patch does not reach it): it is Angevin from March 1279 (ledger) and lost to the Epirotes in 1304-1305. The Corfu page: 'Later in 1294, Corfu was given to Philip I along with the other eastern possessions of the Kingdom of Naples' (Philip of Taranto, a prince of the dynasty), so Corfu passes within the House of Anjou and is kept in this row; the Taranto principality has no Cliopatria row.

correction.text: Corfu plus Durrës (Durazzo) and its surroundings

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1304-1325. 'Angevin forces regained control [of Durrës] after Serbs were expelled in 1304' and 'the Angevins held Durazzo until 1368'; the Cliopatria 1294 patch does not include Durrës. Albanian nobles (Gulielm Blinishti, marshal 1304; Andrea I Muzaka 1318) served the Angevins. Butrint is not in the shape from 1304: the Epirotes recovered it in 1304-1305 (ledger) and the Thomas I page is silent on who held it afterwards.

correction.text: Corfu plus Durrës, until Durrës falls to Thopia in 1368

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1326-1368, which Cliopatria leaves empty for this row: Durazzo stayed Angevin until Karl Thopia took it in 1368 and 'The Thopia and Muzaka families grew in power during the 1320s-1330s and allied with the Angevins against Serbia'. Corfu is kept as in 1304; the page dates no later change.

correction.text: Corfu only (Butrint lost in 1304-1305); page silent, a bridge of the researcher

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1369-1374, which Cliopatria leaves empty: after the loss of Durrës in 1368 the pages opened date nothing Angevin in Albania or Corfu. Corfu is kept as a researcher's bridge (page silent); Achaea comes back in 1373 (ledger). The Corfu page has Corfu passing to Philip I of Taranto in 1294 and controlled by Venice from 1386, with no Angevin loss in between.

union.text: Cliopatria's 1375 shape clipped to the Peloponnese

correction.text: the Principality of Achaea (the Peloponnese) held by Joanna I and then Charles III, 1375-1383, with Corfu; 1381-1383 is held by James of Baux (ledger occupation)

keyframe_review.note: 15,889 km2 in Cliopatria (12,139 km2 at the gazetteer grid), identical to Cliopatria's Principality of Achaea shape of 1314-1325 (bbox to 25.57 E, 39.00 N): this row carries Achaea while the Angevins held it directly. The Achaea page describes the principality as 'rather small, consisting of the Peloponnese peninsula (then known as the Morea)', 'bordered on the north by Epirus and the Duchy of Athens', and does not place central Greece, Euboea or the Cyclades inside it (no area given); the 42 of 48 grid cells that lie in the Peloponnese are kept and the six cells to the north and east are dropped. 'In 1373 Philip II transferred his rights to his cousin Queen Joan I'; 'when Joan was imprisoned in Naples in 1381,' James of Baux 'seized Achaea'; 'In 1383, Achaea was annexed by' Charles III of Naples. Corfu is added as a bridge: the Corfu page has it given to Philip I in 1294 and Venetian from 1386, with no loss between, so it stayed with the dynasty; Cliopatria's shape leaves it out. The row ends in 1384 in Cliopatria and in 1383 here.

union.text: the Albanian coast of the 1279 Cliopatria shape, from Durrës south to Butrint

region.text: the Kingdom of Albania, the Durazzo region south to Butrint, with Corfu

ledger.note: 21 February 1272: Charles I of Anjou is proclaimed King of Albania. 'The Kingdom of Albania was declared in late February 1272' after a treaty with the Albanian nobles and the citizens of Durrës; the kingdom 'ran from the Durazzo region south along the coast to Butrint' (the page gives no firm borders). Gazzo Chinardo was his vicar-general (Charles I page).
1274: Berat goes to the Byzantines. 'Byzantine forces, aided by Albanian nobles, captured the important city of Berat' in 1274; the Angevin siege of 1280-81 failed.

region.text: the Principality of Achaea, the Morea, held through baillis

ledger.note: 1 May 1278: Charles inherits the Principality of Achaea. He 'inherited the Principality of Achaea from William II of Villehardouin, who had died on 1 May 1278' and appointed Galeran of Ivry bailli. Suzerainty over Achaea dated from the Treaty of Viterbo of May 1267.

region.text: the castles of Sopot and Butrint

ledger.note: March 1279: Nikephoros I surrenders Sopot and Butrint. 'In March 1279 Nikephoros I declared himself a vassal of Charles of Anjou and surrendered to him the castles of Sopot and Butrint.' The despotate-of-epirus dossier records the same loss in 1279 (its vassal tint 1279-1281 is for that dossier). Sopot has no coordinate on the page and is carried by the Butrint radius; the earlier keyframe _1272 draws the coast to Butrint as a soft reading.

region.text: the Albanian interior outside the coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint

ledger.note: By 1282: the Albanian interior is lost. 'A Byzantine counteroffensive soon ensued, which drove the Angevins out of the interior by 1282' (Capetian House page); the Kingdom of Albania page says 'by 1281' and has the Angevins still besieging Berat in December 1280, so 1281-1282 is the span and the cited page's year is kept. The kingdom 'was soon reduced by the Albanians to a small area centered around Durrës' (no date). The coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint remain. Cliopatria keeps the interior to 1293.

8 July 1283: Malta passes to Aragon. Roger of Lauria beat the Angevin fleet off Malta and 'received the homage of the city and the island'; Gozo surrendered at once. The Maltese had risen in autumn 1282. Cliopatria drops Malta from 1285. Counterpart changed from crown-of-aragon to kingdom-of-sicily to agree with kingdom-of-sicily.json (ledger 1283, gain of Malta, whose counterpart there is kingdom-of-naples and should be house-of-anjou-sicily, the row whose shape held Malta in 1272-1283): the island kingdom under Peter III of Aragon is the holder; the page names only 'the King of Aragon', not which crown.
1288: Durrës falls to the Byzantines. 'Durrës fell in Byzantine hands in 1288.'

1289: Charles II grants Achaea away. 'after his release and coronation in 1289, [he] granted the Principality to Isabelle of Villehardouin upon her marriage with Florent of Hainaut'; the Angevins keep the suzerainty. Cliopatria resumes its Principality of Achaea row in 1294.
c. 1294: Kaninë, the last Angevin holdout, falls. It fell 'probably in 1294'; Vlorë's fall is not dated.

1304-1305: Butrint goes to Epirus. 'The Epirotes advanced into the Angevin lands in the western Balkans, recovering Butrinto and Naupaktos in 1304-1305'; the page does not say who held Butrinto afterwards (the compromise of 1307 gave Philip of Taranto 'many of the fortresses', not named). Naupaktos and the other Taranto fortresses (the dowry of 1294, Vonitsa and Leucas in 1331) are Philip of Taranto's and Walter of Brienne's lands, which no Cliopatria shape of this row draws; the despotate-of-epirus events of 1294, 1307 and 1331 should name the Taranto line, not this row.
1304: Durrës is Angevin again. 'Angevin forces regained control after Serbs were expelled in 1304' (the Serbian king Stephen Milutin had taken it in 1296).

1368: Karl Thopia takes Durazzo. 'The Angevins held Durazzo until 1368, when Karl Thopia took it with its citizens' consent'; the infobox lists the kingdom as disestablished in 1368 and again 1376-1383 (Louis of Évreux took it in 1376).

1373: Joanna I acquires Achaea. 'In 1373 Philip II transferred his rights to his cousin' Queen Joan I of Naples (James IV of Majorca left her his claim in 1375); Cliopatria resumes this row's Achaea shape in 1375.
1381: James of Baux seizes Achaea. 'when Joan was imprisoned in Naples in 1381,' James of Baux 'used the opportunity and seized Achaea'.
1383: Charles III drives James of Baux out. 'In 1383, Achaea was annexed by Charles III of Naples, and James of Baux was driven away.'

region.text: the row's last shape: Achaea (the Peloponnese) and Corfu

ledger.note: 1383: the Capetian Angevin hold ends. Joanna I's reign ended in 1382 (infobox: 'until 12 May 1382'), Achaea passed to Charles III of Durazzo in 1383 and a Vicary government followed (1383-1396); Cliopatria's row runs to 1384.

wars.name: Siege of Berat (1280-1281)
wars.outcome: The Angevin siege of Berat failed; the Byzantines had held the city since 1274.

wars.name: Byzantine counteroffensive in Angevin Albania

zones.text: the Albanian interior outside the coastal strongholds of Durrës, Vlorë/Kaninë and Butrint

wars.outcome: The Byzantines, aided by Albanian nobles, took Berat (1274), drove the Angevins from the interior by 1282, took Durrës (1288) and probably Kaninë (1294); the Angevins regained Durrës in 1304.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Albania page dates the pieces; the Capetian House page gives 'by 1282' for the interior.

wars.name: Battle of Malta (1283)
wars.outcome: Aragonese victory on 8 July 1283 (some sources: 8 June); Roger of Lauria received the homage of Malta and Gozo.
wars.note: Part of the War of the Sicilian Vespers, which began on 30 March 1282 and ended Charles's rule in Sicily (Charles I page).

wars.name: Serbian conquest of Durrës
wars.outcome: Stephen Milutin took Durrës in 1296; the Angevins regained it after the Serbs were expelled in 1304.

wars.name: Epirote recovery of Butrint and Naupaktos
wars.outcome: The Epirotes recovered Butrinto and Naupaktos in 1304-1305; an Angevin invasion of 1307 ended in a compromise that ceded 'many of the fortresses' to Philip of Taranto.

wars.name: Seizure of Achaea by James of Baux
wars.outcome: James of Baux seized Achaea in 1381; Charles III of Naples annexed it in 1383 and drove him away.

certainty.note: The Kingdom of Albania's borders 'were poorly defined' (Kingdom of Albania page); the Achaean frontier and the Cliopatria patches are approximate; no treaty line is dated.

notes: Shares Wikidata Q939200 with capetian-house-of-anjou. Merge test: NOT merged, as that dossier already concluded: Cliopatria's 'Capetian House of Anjou' draws Anjou, Maine and Provence in France, this row draws the Angevin lands in Albania, Corfu, Malta and Achaea (the dynasty's overseas holdings), and the two rows never overlap. This row is not a state in the usual sense: it is a bag of Angevin-held lands that Cliopatria draws when they were held directly by the dynasty: 1272-1278 Corfu, 1279-1293 the Achaea shape plus Albania, Corfu and Malta (the Cliopatria Principality of Achaea row has a gap in 1279-1293 and again in 1326-1384), 1294-1325 a 725 km2 coastal patch (the same cells Cliopatria later gives the Principality of Valona), 1375-1384 the Achaea shape again (identical to Achaea's 1314-1325 shape). The Angevin Kingdom of Albania (1272-1368) and the Angevin Principality of Achaea are two Wikipedia states; a gap-filler may prefer to give each its own dossier (new slugs kingdom-of-albania-angevin and the Achaea dossier of eu-05, which should record Charles I's direct rule 1278-1289). No page gives an area figure, so the check of Cliopatria's Area against an infobox was not possible. The 1375 shape's bbox reaches central Greece and the Cyclades; the Achaea page does not support that and the Achaea dossier should be asked. Pages silent on: when Corfu passed from the Angevins (held to at least 1292 per the Albania page; Cliopatria shows nothing after 1325 until 1375, and the Valona row takes the patch from 1333), Charles's Latin Empire rights, the Kingdom of Albania after 1368 (Louis of Évreux 1376, Thopia 1383, Balša II 1385, Venice 1392), Navarrese Company and the Duchy of Athens. Gazetteer names needed: none new. Counterparts as persons: 'James of Baux' and 'Karl Thopia (Principality of Albania)' (Albanian Principalities row starts 1375). The 1283 Malta loss: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sicily 1272-1278 shape also reaches 35.77 N, so the island is double-drawn in 1272-1278; the kingdom-of-sicily dossier should confirm. Repairs of 2026-10-25 (review eu-18-d): keyframes now follow the ledger step by step (_1279 valid 1279-1281; new _1282, _1283, _1285 valid 1285-1287, _1288, _1289 for 1289-1293 = the coastal patch plus Butrint); the March 1279 gain of Sopot and Butrint from the Despotate of Epirus and the 1304-1305 loss of Butrint to the Epirotes are mirrored; the 1282 date follows the Capetian House page ('by 1282'), the Kingdom of Albania page says 'by 1281'. The capital is Durrës (1272-1288, 1304-1368) and Corfu in the other years, because Naples lies outside every shape. Malta 1283: counterpart is now kingdom-of-sicily; the kingdom-of-sicily dossier (eu-12) has the gain from kingdom-of-naples at confidence 1 and should name house-of-anjou-sicily. The Taranto line's lands are outside this row: Corfu is given to Philip I of Taranto in 1294 (kept here because Cliopatria's patch carries it), but the 1294 dowry fortresses, the 1307 compromise, Naupaktos, and Walter of Brienne's Vonitsa and Leucas of 1331 (despotate-of-epirus ledger 33, 35, 39) are Philip's and Walter's, and that dossier should change its counterpart (there is no Cliopatria row for the Principality of Taranto). The 1375 keyframe is clipped to the Peloponnese (the Achaea page: 'rather small, consisting of the Peloponnese peninsula') and given Corfu as a bridge (Corfu page: Venetian from 1386). Gazetteer names needed: Butrint (place, 39.75 N, 20.02 E, used as a coordinate), Kaninë (place near Vlorë).
